The citation's human half goes on the wire — `cited`, additive and optional
No normative write surface, ever; a companion note after it is built
`[[id]]` is a plain internal link and is silent on the wire
Staleness is a direct relation; nothing on the wire is missing
`generator_url` — an optional manifest key naming the client's source; no maintenance declaration
Identity practice: URL-shaped, proven by reciprocal link or signature over `content_hash`; a recommended practice, never protocol
Groups: no new construct; two supported shapes and a test; content-free stubbing is an anti-pattern
Imported generated text is disclosed through the existing `generated[]`; the draft's rule 7 was wrong and is replaced
The protocol is agent-agnostic at every level, and says so; the response-versus-pipe line is what matters, not human-versus-agent
A minimal reference agent is worth building; the contract it proves is the product; RAG hooks already exist; attribution level is the author's choice, not the agent's capability
Changelog notes: depth is bounded by what is public; generated notes are a studio default and disclosed by a flag; the narrative is reader-side
Discovery through stub chains: four client surfaces need nothing from the spec; forward discovery is closed by #28, and the one addition that would open it is a 0.4 candidate
Publication guidance: implement the published living text, pin to snapshots, never build from plan docs or client code; ruled shapes appear in the living spec's §16 before they are built
Version boundary rule: revisions add what readers already ignore safely; a new version is needed when a reader or receiver must change what it does
Remote generation sources: a source, not a quotation, disclosed as a reference, and it notifies — a fourth mention relation `source`; a 0.4 construct written before its build, deliberately
Transitive staleness does not exist and will not be defined
No title field, at any version; the wish is met by the derived title and by presentation
Two parked feed/surface candidates decided against: pinned-content feed entries not opened; the per-item responses surface stays closed
Conformance partition for the suite (roadmap-tracks 1.4, the Fable half)
Partial quotation is a partial *transclusion* — same directive family, a text-quote selector, substring-verified — and it is a 0.3 revision, not a 0.4 construct
A reader affordance that inserts `[[id]]` does not collide with #27, because a link is not a response; it must be named for what it does and kept out of the response slot

The manifest locates the surface: `feed`/`items` become authoritative, `item`/`pin` URI templates are added, a manifest need not be named `blyg.json` when HTML can point at it, and identity is the manifest's URL minus its last segment — a 0.4 construct
An OAuth-style minting flow stays within #31; MCP is a transport for #39's contract, not a second one; the contributor builds 2.9 and Opus comes off it
`content_html` is self-contained: every URL in it absolute
`[[id]]` is inert inside code, as the directive already was
`cited` MAY sit on a `{url}` stub
`page` SHOULD be stable for the life of an item

A fork of a thread descends from the pinned document, not from its composition: baked quotes are flattened into ordinary blockquotes with an attribution line, recursively, and the fork inherits no `transclusions[]`
Model routing gates on blast radius, not topic: Opus 5.5 rules reversible questions under a four-question test and Fable reviews in batch; Fable keeps what reaches the wire

density.heading: Historical versions: pinned-only, JSON promised, HTML optional
The watermark, history rewrites, and stealth edits
L0 grandfathering — the legacy RSS wrapper
Webmention — response notification with structural verification
What a verified mention is, and is not

lowercase_modals.text: No data attributes are required: span-level source mapping is deliberately not promised (the JSON provenance is version-level and robust; span-level claims would be brittle across the author's post-generation edits).

This derivation is documented so that the same item reads the same in different plain-RSS readers; a client that derives differently is conformant but should know that it is choosing to make its items read differently elsewhere.
Publishers should understand pins are irrevocable before pinning, and should understand that anything published can be quoted into a thread whose snapshot they cannot recall.
Readers that care about ordering across origins must apply their own observation-time policy (§13.7).
It may still *send* — a static export is produced by some dynamic studio, which can send at export time — but is not required to.

absolutes.text: May be a domain root, any path under a domain, or a subdomain — the protocol never constrains where a blyg mounts (§4).

**Every L2 construct is additive and optional to emit**: a valid 0.2 document is a valid 0.3 document unchanged, and a publisher that never quotes another origin, never stubs, never forks, and receives no mentions is fully conformant at L2 by doing nothing new.
Vocabulary evolves inside one namespace under those ignore rules; a breaking change, if one ever happens, gets a major version bump and its own migration story — never this mechanism.
Ids are never content-addressed — editing changes content, not identity.
The `changelog` is metadata (version, time, optional note, optional `"pinned": true`), never diffs or content.
**A note describes a change; it never reproduces withheld content.**
Authors are **never addressable**: no protocol construct references an author, at any level, permanently.
Invariant 3 stands: AI is never in the protocol.
At 0.3 a source is always own-origin and carries no `origin` member; generation from another origin's items is not expressible on the wire at this version.
Disclosure covers what was produced and from what, never how it was asked for.
Drawn-upon material is woven into new prose, not quoted: source references never appear in `transclusions` and never produce a `blyg-transclusion` blockquote.
The key is omitted entirely when the version involved no generation, and a withdrawal endcap (§9) never carries it.
The reference client always emits it.
`origin` is the target's **identity origin** as §12.2 defines it — the post-redirect URL the target's manifest was fetched from, minus `blyg.json` — never the target manifest's self-asserted `site`.

It is **self-asserted and never authoritative**, like every other provenance member in this protocol, and it is **frozen at the moment the reference was made** — publish time for a transclusion, which is re-resolved at every publish (§10.2); creation time for `stub_of` and `forked_from`.
The `site` value is self-asserted and display-advisory only; it never establishes identity (§12.2).

**There is deliberately no maintained/unmaintained declaration**: the software that would need to say "I am unmaintained" is exactly the software nobody is updating, so maintenance status is a fact for directories to observe, never for the wire to assert.
The opaque `author` object itself never appears in the XML: the state plane is ground truth, the feed is a signal.
It never tracks the protocol version: the `0.1` inside it is part of the spelling, not a version claim, and it stays unchanged across protocol versions.
Later versions add elements to this same namespace under the reader ignore rule (§13.1); the protocol version signal is the manifest's `blyg` key (§3.1), never the namespace.
`content_hash` covers `content_md` only, so the pin's immutability guarantee covers *content*, never the author bytes.
Keep each pinned version discrete, visibly frozen, and individually citable; a presentation cannot reconstruct a continuous edit history, because the bytes for one are never served.
The route exposes only bytes already promised forever — never unpinned history.
(Discarding a never-published draft is a hard delete — nothing was ever public.)
For threads, the endcap also empties `transclusions` to `[]` (§10.4) and omits `stub_of` (§10.6); an endcap never carries a `generated` array (§5.7).

**At 0.3 both restrictions are lifted**: a thread may transclude fragments or threads, of its own origin or of any origin its publisher has imported — and the rule that makes this safe is that the quote is always the publisher's **local snapshot**, never a live fetch.
An unresolvable link is a publish error, like an unresolvable directive.
Resolution happens in the studio at publish time; **readers never resolve anything**.
otherwise a **publish error**.
**More than one imported match is a publish error**, never a guess — the directive names an identity, and the publisher does not pick an origin on the author's behalf.
**The local snapshot is what gets baked — never a live fetch.**
**Publish never depends on the network.**

A source that has since been withdrawn at its origin, and not pin-retained, is a publish error on republish — exactly as a withdrawn local fragment is — and the author removes the directive or leaves the thread at its current version.

`origin` is **omitted for own-origin sources** — every 0.2 thread document is therefore a valid 0.3 document unchanged — and for remote sources is the subscription's identity origin (§12.2), never the source manifest's self-asserted `site`.
Mention verification (§15.4) ignores it, as it ignores `cited`; a reader that ignores it entirely remains conformant, because readers display baked HTML and never resolve.
Fragments omit the key entirely; threads always carry it (a withdrawn thread's endcap carries `[]`).
Generation sources are disclosed separately and never appear here (§5.7), and a plain internal link (§10.1) produces no entry: only copied words are disclosed.

Threads only — the frozen v0 concept's own framing ("stubs are threads, so a stack always looks like a link to a local thread"), and what makes stubs stackable: threads can be transcluded, so a stub of a stub is nesting, not a new construct.
The protocol never requires the body to transclude the target.
`stub_of` is the machine-readable response marker, and readers rely on it, never on body inspection.

(The reference client's stub action always starts the body with `![[id]]` for a blyg target, because a stub without the quote is not a stub in the medium's own aesthetic; an author who deletes the directive has still published a stub.)
The two can never disagree on a published document.
**One hop only**: a rel target's own HTML is never scanned — no recursive discovery, no loops.
Poll failure never justifies discarding stored state (§13.2).
Rollup is driven by version numbers, never timestamps.
**Malformed input degrades; it never corrupts.**
The feed never mutates state directly: an interesting entry — including a withdrawal entry — triggers an item-document fetch, and **only the fetched document advances state**.
The highest version ever observed per imported item is a monotonic **watermark**, and it never silently regresses:
**Imported items are never re-emitted.**
Publicity is a property of the displayed *list*, never of an imported item.
It never re-emits, and it never stubs on the members' behalf (§10.6).
An L0 row is never a transclusion source (§10.2); a response to an L0 entry is a `{url}` stub (§10.6).
Ordering the merged reading surface is the reader's own policy, never the protocol's — remote timestamps are self-asserted (§5.2) and comparable only advisorily.
It is therefore per-item curation (§15.5), never automatic.
The reference endpoint is `{origin}webmention` — *inside* the origin surface, because it is a protocol surface, unlike a studio or its API, which are host-rooted client internals and never protocol.
Same-origin references never generate mentions.
A claim refused by any cap is 429 and is never queued.
They are never auto-published, never enter the feed, the archive index, or any item document, and add no manifest vocabulary.

5.title: AI is never in the protocol

7.title: Private content in v1 = never-published drafts

19.title: Versioning stays a bare counter; pins are the significance primitive

21.title: Development-phase strategy: pre-1.0 spec is always draft; 1.0 is the release event

22.title: Namespace URI is a permanent opaque token

23.title: Per-version spec documents; the highest version is the living one

25.title: §8.4 constrains routes and promises, not presentation; the pinned-version carousel conforms

27.title: Stubs are threads with `stub_of`; the stub action absorbs `respond`

29.title: The `page` field closes the permalink-convention gap

30.title: The citation's human half goes on the wire — `cited`, additive and optional

31.title: No normative write surface, ever; a companion note after it is built

32.title: `[[id]]` is a plain internal link and is silent on the wire

33.title: Staleness is a direct relation; nothing on the wire is missing

34.title: `generator_url` — an optional manifest key naming the client's source; no maintenance declaration

35.title: Identity practice: URL-shaped, proven by reciprocal link or signature over `content_hash`; a recommended practice, never protocol

36.title: Groups: no new construct; two supported shapes and a test; content-free stubbing is an anti-pattern

37.title: Imported generated text is disclosed through the existing `generated[]`; the draft's rule 7 was wrong and is replaced

38.title: The protocol is agent-agnostic at every level, and says so; the response-versus-pipe line is what matters, not human-versus-agent

39.title: A minimal reference agent is worth building; the contract it proves is the product; RAG hooks already exist; attribution level is the author's choice, not the agent's capability

40.title: Changelog notes: depth is bounded by what is public; generated notes are a studio default and disclosed by a flag; the narrative is reader-side

41.title: Discovery through stub chains: four client surfaces need nothing from the spec; forward discovery is closed by #28, and the one addition that would open it is a 0.4 candidate

42.title: Publication guidance: implement the published living text, pin to snapshots, never build from plan docs or client code; ruled shapes appear in the living spec's §16 before they are built

43.title: Version boundary rule: revisions add what readers already ignore safely; a new version is needed when a reader or receiver must change what it does

44.title: Remote generation sources: a source, not a quotation, disclosed as a reference, and it notifies — a fourth mention relation `source`; a 0.4 construct written before its build, deliberately

45.title: Transitive staleness does not exist and will not be defined

46.title: No title field, at any version; the wish is met by the derived title and by presentation

47.title: Two parked feed/surface candidates decided against: pinned-content feed entries not opened; the per-item responses surface stays closed

48.title: Conformance partition for the suite (roadmap-tracks 1.4, the Fable half)

49.title: Partial quotation is a partial *transclusion* — same directive family, a text-quote selector, substring-verified — and it is a 0.3 revision, not a 0.4 construct

50.title: A reader affordance that inserts `[[id]]` does not collide with #27, because a link is not a response; it must be named for what it does and kept out of the response slot

51.title: The manifest locates the surface: `feed`/`items` become authoritative, `item`/`pin` URI templates are added, a manifest need not be named `blyg.json` when HTML can point at it, and identity is the manifest's URL minus its last segment — a 0.4 construct

52.title: An OAuth-style minting flow stays within #31; MCP is a transport for #39's contract, not a second one; the contributor builds 2.9 and Opus comes off it

53.title: `content_html` is self-contained: every URL in it absolute

54.title: `[[id]]` is inert inside code, as the directive already was

56.title: `page` SHOULD be stable for the life of an item

57.title: A fork of a thread descends from the pinned document, not from its composition: baked quotes are flattened into ordinary blockquotes with an attribution line, recursively, and the fork inherits no `transclusions[]`

58.title: Model routing gates on blast radius, not topic: Opus 5.5 rules reversible questions under a four-question test and Fable reviews in batch; Fable keeps what reaches the wire
